hypothesis: An explicit role-routing checklist improves ownership/action decisions beyond current post-adoption guidance. No improvement is a valid result.
sampling: One fresh process per condition, all six cases in identical order; no retries selected by answer quality; baseline launched before checklist.

scoring.unit: one binary pass per dimension per case, 36 per condition; count change-owner accuracy separately
scoring.method: Human-readable author assessment using answer_key.json, with concise quotations and independent review. Accept equivalent existing doors and role names. Context pass requires relevant listed follow-up scope without whole-ecosystem loading; does not measure actual retrieval.
scoring.failure: Wrong/unsupported owner, invented role/door, violated approval/science boundary, or broad unrelated context is a fail on the affected dimension. Malformed output is reported, not silently repaired.

decision_rule: No net correctness gain and no clear minimal-context gain => do not mandate checklist. Any gain is hypothesis-generating only; recommend a larger fresh-context/real-task comparison before production changes. No additional framework or organs from this trial.
limitations: same fixed order, possible within-response learning
same model and authored expected key
no real retrieval, execution or token-cost efficiency measurement
explicit source guidance may cause ceiling effects
CLI runtime has common ambient workspace instructions; tools and MCP disabled, no other files retrievable
no seed guarantee; stochastic/session variation not separated from intervention
shared structured answer fields already scaffold producer/owner/door reasoning in both conditions; tests marginal checklist value under that scaffold
working_directory: PyAutoBrain worktree; both fresh processes use same cwd
